access.edition_or_version: Oxford World's Classics, trans. Henry Chadwick (1991)

mechanics.tone_relevance: Founds the addressed first-person confession: the narrating self is examined and disclosed to a witness (God), with the reader positioned as an overhearer.
mechanics.point_of_view: First person, retrospective narrator addressing a 'you' throughout; the address constitutes the intimacy.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Restless desire and error, recalled shame, and eventual submission; disclosure escalates from childhood mischief to adult spiritual crisis.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Direct address and apostrophe; scriptural quotation woven into personal narration; self-interrogation and rhetorical questioning.
mechanics.dialogue: Frequent quoted address to God and to the reader's understanding, converting narration into a two-sided exchange.
mechanics.imagery: Concrete sensory memories (the pear theft, the garden) used to anchor abstract self-examination.
mechanics.intimacy_technique: Self-accusation performed before a witness; the disclosure is offered as truth about the self rather than as information.
mechanics.duration_and_dosage: Long-form, graduated exposure across books rather than a single maximal disclosure.
mechanics.critical_reception: Canonical origin point of the Western confessional tradition.
mechanics.copyright_note: Original Latin public domain; English translation copyrighted. Techniques described, no text reproduced.
